description: Astroboys are a team of computer science students specializing in software engineering. The members have scholarly experience in programming, videography, graphic design, and prompt engineering. The team is interested in mapping martian soil and the present hazards it may bring during manned missions.
summary: MapaMars turns NASA's separate Mars datasets into one layered map that helps an astronaut plan a safe, scientifically useful Marswalk and then follow it on foot. An astronaut explores Jezero Crater from whole-planet scale down to 25 cm per pixel, clicks any point for its elevation, slope, hazards, nearby science targets and real Perseverance photos, then plans a walk between science stops. MapaMars finds a safe path round steep, deep and rocky ground (A* search over NASA elevation models) and shows the distance, walking time, climb, steepest slope, return-to-base margin, an elevation profile and an estimated radiation dose. An EVA mode turns the route into a simple, high-contrast view for walking it: the next stop, the time back to base and one alert at a time. Routes can be saved as missions with a code and shared with a crew. Every number is labelled Observed, Derived, or Estimated, so the crew knows what it can trust.
details:
What it does

- Explore: a 3D globe and a 2D NASA map of all of Mars, with walking-scale imagery at Jezero Crater. Layers are grouped into Topographic, Optical, and Spectral, and you can switch them on and off. Clicking open ground shows its coordinates, elevation, slope, terrain hazards (Topographic), the nearest science targets, Perseverance photos, and map tile enhancement (Optical), including heat and Brightness, Mineral Spectroscopy, and dust indices (Spectral).

- Plan a Marswalk: place a start, waypoints and science stops. MAPA routes round slopes too steep to walk, hollows too deep to climb out of and rocky ground, and shades that ground so the crew can see why. It gives distance, walking time, height gained and lost, steepest slope, the EVA return margin, a radiation estimate and science opportunities near the route.

- EVA mode: the route as walked in a suit, with three facts, one alert at a time (turn back, sunset, steep ground ahead) and large buttons.

- Missions: save a route with a code like MRS-204, share it with a crew and keep a mission log. No sign-up needed.

How it works

React and TypeScript in the browser, OpenLayers for the 2D map and three.js for the globe. Map tiles come from NASA Mars Trek through a server-side allow-list proxy. Elevation comes from the USGS Jezero CTX elevation model (20 m) and global MOLA (463 m); rocky ground comes from HiRISE elevation models (1 m). An A* search in a web worker finds the safe path. Day and night, Mars time and Sun position are calculated live; moon and orbiter positions come from NASA JPL Horizons. Missions are stored in Supabase with row-level security.

Benefits

Today's Mars tools are regional or global. MapaMars works at the scale of one walk, puts safety first, and combines topographic, optical, and spectral data in one place. It shows where each number comes from, so a crew can tell what is measured and what is assumed.

Tools: React, TypeScript, Vite, OpenLayers, three.js, geotiff.js, Supabase, Vercel.
